decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already records that the Hero V must be resolved before its geometry is used to develop the second V.
The existing DEFER captures lifecycle state, but the source also establishes the durable prerequisite that the Hero V must be settled before its geometry is used to develop the É accent.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The iterative studies have made the direction much clearer: the identity is emerging from the relationship between the V’s two arms, not from the accent or any decorative detail. At this stage, small geometric adjustments should have far more impact than introducing additional concepts.

Please keep resolving the hero V rather than branching into new concepts or developing the complete V system. For the right arm, continue testing a construction that differs from the left through proportion and geometry, not through added styling. At the same time, simplify the left arm by moving away from a conventional Roman flare toward a cleaner, more precisely resolved termination. That change could strengthen the contrast between the two sides without making the letter decorative.

Continue refining this construction until it feels fully resolved. Only once the hero V is settled should its geometry be used to develop the second V, the É accent, and eventually the remainder of the wordmark. When the hero V feels right, the rest of the identity system should follow naturally.
